title: Gauge invariance, collective modes, and the justification of normal-state subtraction in Dirac superconductors
abstract: In Dirac superconductors, the unbounded spectrum of low-energy Dirac models is known to give rise to unphysical interband contributions from deep-lying states to the electromagnetic response. To eliminate these contributions, normal-state subtraction (NSS), in which the normal-state response is subtracted from the superconducting-state response, has been widely employed. However, the relation between NSS and a gauge-invariant electromagnetic response, particularly the role of the vertex correction required by the Ward identity, has remained unclear. In this work, we consider a massive-Dirac model with $s$-wave pairing and analytically investigate the electromagnetic response at zero temperature by solving the Bethe--Salpeter equation and incorporating the collective-mode contribution to the electromagnetic vertex. We show that, in the static long-wavelength limit, the vertex correction exactly cancels the bare longitudinal response with NSS, yielding the vanishing longitudinal response required by gauge invariance. In contrast, the transverse component of the vertex correction vanishes in the long-wavelength limit, so that the gauge-invariant Meissner weight coincides with that obtained from the bare transverse response with NSS. Moreover, within the class of isotropic and analytic UV regularization terms, we show that gauge invariance uniquely fixes the regularization term in the static long-wavelength limit to the value prescribed by NSS. Our results thus provide a microscopic justification for NSS.
summary: This theoretical work addresses the ambiguity in calculating the electromagnetic response of Dirac superconductors by investigating the role of vertex corrections. The authors demonstrate that the Normal-State Subtraction (NSS) procedure is rigorously justified because the vertex correction exactly restores gauge invariance in the static limit. This provides a crucial microscopic foundation for a widely used approximation in superconducting theory.
main_problem: The paper aims to microscopically justify the use of Normal-State Subtraction (NSS) when calculating the gauge-invariant electromagnetic response in Dirac superconductors.
main_result: The vertex correction exactly cancels the bare longitudinal response with NSS in the static long-wavelength limit, satisfying the required gauge invariance condition. This confirms that NSS is a valid theoretical procedure for this system.
method: The authors use linear response theory, solving the Bethe-Salpeter equation, and analyzing the electromagnetic response kernel in the static, long-wavelength limit.
model_or_system: The system studied is a Dirac superconductor, modeled using a massive-Dirac Hamiltonian with s-wave pairing. The analysis involves calculating the current-current correlation function via the Kubo formula.
key_observables: Longitudinal ($\Phi_L$) and transverse ($\Phi_T$) components of the electromagnetic response kernel, and the Meissner weight.
important_parameters: Static long-wavelength limit ($\omega=0, q 	o 0$), superconducting gap ($\Delta$), and the normal-state response ($\Phi_N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the UV regularization term can be treated as an additive contribution, and it focuses on the static, long-wavelength limit to enforce gauge invariance.
paper_structure: The paper develops the full response kernel by decomposing it into bare, UV regularization, and vertex correction terms. It then analyzes the longitudinal and transverse components separately, showing how the vertex correction enforces gauge invariance when NSS is applied.
why_interesting: While focused on superconductivity, the rigorous application of gauge invariance constraints via vertex corrections and the justification of a subtraction scheme (NSS) is a fundamental theoretical technique applicable to many interacting quantum systems.
